definition: Iteratively training a model using labels or outputs generated by itself or a related model.
example: Use confident predictions to expand training data.
caveat: It can reinforce the model's own mistakes.

definition: Choosing chunk boundaries using meaning, discourse structure, or semantic similarity.
example: Keep related paragraphs together.
caveat: The segmentation criterion can be unstable or expensive.

definition: Stored general facts or summarized knowledge made available to a system.
example: Retrieve a user's stated project requirements.
caveat: Stored statements need provenance and may become outdated.

definition: Retrieval intended to match meaning rather than only exact words.
example: Find paraphrases of a query.
caveat: Semantic similarity does not guarantee task relevance.

definition: Assigning a category label to each pixel without separating individual objects of the same class.
example: Label road, sky, and vehicle pixels.
caveat: Two neighboring cars can share the same semantic label.

definition: Learning with a combination of labeled and unlabeled examples.
example: Combine 500 labeled images with many unlabeled images.
caveat: Incorrect pseudo-labels can reinforce errors.

definition: A vector representing a sentence or passage for comparison or prediction.
example: Retrieve semantically related sentences.
caveat: Pooling a generic language model is not always a strong sentence embedder.

definition: A tokenization toolkit supporting models such as BPE and Unigram directly over raw text.
example: Train a tokenizer without presegmented word inputs.
caveat: SentencePiece is a library/framework, not one unique algorithm.

definition: The number of sequence elements processed in a model input or computation.
example: Train on sequences of 2,048 tokens.
caveat: It may include padding or exclude it depending on reporting.

definition: Combining multiple examples into longer training sequences to reduce wasted space.
example: Pack short conversations into a full token block.
caveat: Boundaries and attention leakage between examples need explicit handling.

definition: Adding placeholder positions so variable-length sequences can share tensor shapes.
example: Batch texts of unequal lengths.
caveat: Padding positions often need masking in both attention and loss.

definition: Partitioning work or activations along the sequence dimension to reduce replicated memory or computation.
example: Distribute long-sequence transformer processing.
caveat: The name covers several implementation-specific schemes.

definition: Training on complete sequences generated or selected by a teacher.
example: Train a small translator on teacher translations.
caveat: Generated sequences can reduce diversity or propagate errors.

definition: A framework mapping one sequence to another, often using encoder and decoder components.
example: Translate a sentence into another language.
caveat: Input and output lengths can differ.

definition: Running a candidate alongside the active system without using its outputs for user-facing decisions.
example: Compare a new model on realistic traffic.
caveat: Shadow observations may not capture consequences of acting on the output.

definition: A family of feature-attribution methods based on Shapley-value ideas and chosen background assumptions.
example: Explain a prediction with feature contributions.
caveat: The background distribution and dependence assumptions affect results.

definition: A cooperative-game allocation rule averaging a participant's marginal contribution across coalitions.
example: Allocate predictive contribution among features.
caveat: Computational approximations and feature-dependence choices matter.

definition: Learning an easy predictive cue instead of the intended underlying relationship.
example: Classify images using backgrounds rather than objects.
caveat: A shortcut may perform well until the environment changes.

definition: Behavior that prevents or circumvents an intended shutdown mechanism.
example: Evaluate whether a task-focused agent resists interruption.
caveat: Observed avoidance needs careful attribution and a clear threat model.

definition: The ability to reliably stop a system through an authorized mechanism without problematic resistance.
example: Test an agent's response to a stop signal.
caveat: Reliable system-level stopping requires external controls.

definition: A function mapping real inputs into the interval zero to one.
example: Convert a binary-classification logit into a probability.
caveat: Extreme inputs can yield very small gradients.

definition: A measure comparing the magnitude or power of a desired signal with that of noise.
example: Describe corruption strength during diffusion training.
caveat: The exact signal and noise definitions must be specified.

definition: A clustering score comparing within-cluster distance with distance to the nearest alternative cluster.
example: Assess separation in a proposed clustering.
caveat: It can favor particular cluster shapes and depends on the metric.

definition: An activation multiplying an input by its sigmoid.
example: Use a smooth gated activation in neural blocks.
caveat: Swish can also refer to variants with a scale parameter.

definition: Factoring a matrix into orthogonal directions and nonnegative singular values.
example: Construct a low-rank matrix approximation.
caveat: Truncated SVD keeps only selected components.

definition: Fixed position features built from sine and cosine functions at different frequencies.
example: Provide positions in the original Transformer design.
caveat: It is different from rotating query/key vectors.

definition: A model's ability to represent relevant facts about its identity, deployment, training, or evaluation situation.
example: Test whether behavior changes with perceived oversight.
caveat: Correct descriptions may be pattern matching rather than robust self-understanding.

definition: A Word2Vec objective predicting surrounding words from a center word.
example: Learn vectors from local word neighborhoods.
caveat: Context-window choices influence learned relationships.

definition: A model with behavior that changes under a designated trigger, studied as a proxy for hidden harmful behavior.
example: Evaluate a deliberately constructed conditional backdoor.
caveat: Constructed research examples do not show the same behavior arises universally.

definition: Attention restricted to a moving neighborhood of positions.
example: Bound local attention computation and cache usage.
caveat: Stacked layers may propagate information beyond one local window.

definition: A comparatively compact language model designed for lower resource costs or narrower deployment needs.
example: Run a specialized assistant on local hardware.
caveat: Small is relative; no universally fixed size boundary.

definition: Creating minority-class feature vectors by interpolating between nearby minority examples.
example: Balance a tabular training set.
caveat: Interpolated points may not be semantically valid.

definition: Trainable continuous vectors supplied as a prompt-like input.
example: Represent task instructions with learned embeddings.
caveat: They need not correspond to readable vocabulary tokens.

definition: Probability distributions or continuous targets carrying more information than a single hard label.
example: Match a teacher's class probabilities.
caveat: Low-probability classes can convey useful relative structure.

definition: An SVM allowing margin violations with a penalty.
example: Fit noisy data that is not perfectly separable.
caveat: The penalty controls a tradeoff, not absolute error prevention.

definition: A transformation converting a vector of scores into normalized positive probabilities.
example: Produce a vocabulary distribution from logits.
caveat: Softmax probabilities are not automatically calibrated.

definition: Corrupting contiguous token spans and training a model to recover missing content.
example: Pretrain a text-to-text model.
caveat: Span length and corruption format affect the objective.

definition: Attention permitting only a subset of all possible position interactions.
example: Scale to longer sequences with structured connectivity.
caveat: Reduced connectivity changes information flow.

definition: An autoencoder trained with sparse internal activations, often used to discover features in model representations.
example: Decompose hidden states into sparse feature activations.
caveat: Recovered features can be incomplete, split, or hard to interpret.

definition: Representing data with only a small number of active coefficients in a chosen or learned dictionary.
example: Encode hidden activations sparsely.
caveat: Sparse representations are not automatically semantic.

definition: A feature representation containing mostly zeros.
example: A document's bag-of-words vector.
caveat: Sparse storage and sparse information are not identical.

definition: A compute routine that exploits a specified sparsity pattern to avoid some operations or memory accesses.
example: Accelerate supported structured-sparse matrix multiplication.
caveat: Zeros do not save computation unless the execution path exploits them.

definition: A matrix stored or treated in terms of its relatively few nonzero entries.
example: Store a large document-term matrix efficiently.
caveat: Some operations can unexpectedly produce dense results.

definition: A model using sparse weights, sparse activations, or selective computation, depending on context.
example: Activate a small subset of MoE experts.
caveat: Specify which notion of sparsity is intended.

definition: Retrieval using sparse term-based or learned sparse representations.
example: Search with BM25 or sparse neural vectors.
caveat: Sparse does not necessarily mean non-neural.

definition: A reward signal occurring only rarely or after long action sequences.
example: Reward only complete task success.
caveat: Sparse reward makes exploration and credit assignment harder.

definition: Values added around input boundaries to control how local operations handle edges and output size.
example: Preserve image dimensions through a convolution.
caveat: Spatial padding differs from adding padding tokens to sequences.

definition: A reserved marker with a structural or control role beyond ordinary text content.
example: Mark sequence boundaries or speaker roles.
caveat: Its meaning depends on the tokenizer and training template.

definition: Satisfying a formal or measured objective in a way that misses the intended goal.
example: Exploit a scoring loophole instead of completing the task.
caveat: Undesired behavior can arise without deliberate deception.

definition: The fraction of actual negative cases correctly classified as negative.
example: Measure how often normal cases avoid false alarms.
caveat: Specificity is not the same as precision.
